JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
2.

The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 29-08-2022 at about 3.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Bullet Bike bearing No. KA-50-V-7377, from Rajanukunte, on the extreme left side of the road, on Madure road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.
When he reached Dibbur Gate, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, Bengaluru District

, suddenly the driver of car bearing No. KA-50-MB-4388 came from behind i.e., from Rajanukunte towards Byatha side, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Chiguru Multispeciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 29-08-2022 at about 3.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Bullet Bike bearing No. KA-50-V-7377, from Rajanukunte, on the extreme left side of the road, on Madure road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition and got marked total 26 documents as Ex.P.1 to 26.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.5 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is discharge summary, Ex.P.8 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.9 is notarised copy of driving licence, Ex.P.10 is true copy of Registration Certificate, Ex.P.11 is true copy of insurance policy, Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total24), Ex.P.13 are prescriptions (total 2),
Ex.P.14 are advance receipts (total 4), Ex.P.15 is out-patient record, Ex.P.16 is notarised copy of ID card, Ex.P.17 is notarised copy of police intimation, Ex.P.18 is notarized copy of MLC extract,

Ex.P.19 is original case sheet, Ex.P.20 are x-rays (total 3), Ex.P.21 is clinical examination report,

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending vehicle, issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.
Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained unrebutted.

Though, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the said facts in its written statement, they have not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even the respondent No.1 & 2 have not step into witness box to deposed the contentions taken in their written statement on oath.

There is no evidence on record to show that,

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, on 29-08- 2022 at about 3.45 p.m., near Dibbur Gate, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Yelahanka Taluk, Bengaluru District, when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing No. KA-50-V- 7377, slowly and cautiously, on the extreme left side of the road, from Rajanukunte towards Byatha side, the driver of car bearing No.KA-50-MB-4388, came from behind, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
14. The Ex.P.3 spot mahazer clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on extreme left of 25 feet width Rajanukunte-Madhure main road.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-50-MB- 4388 and dashing to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind, the said accident has taken place and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of his body.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
Ex.P.19 case sheet, Ex.P.20 x-rays (total 3), Ex.P.21 clinical examination report, Ex.P.22 x-ray and Ex.P.24 case-sheet, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered fracture of the left rib 3rd to 8th ribs, fracture of the right humerus fracture with high radial nerve palsy.
The same has been deposed by the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has clinically examined and assessed the disability of the petitioner.

On the other hand,
the respondents No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence to substantiate the contentions taken in their written statements.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.
KA-50-MB-4388 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
16.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-50-MB-4388.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has caused due to self rash and negligent driving of petitioner and not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-50-MB-4388.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

sentences.text: Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635,

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

No.KA-50- MB-4388.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No. KA- 50-MB-4388 and he has sustained fracture of the left rib 3 rd to 8th ribs, fracture of the right humerus fracture with high radial nerve palsy and for the said injuries he has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8, the date of birth of the petitioner is 15-05-1980.
The accident has taken place on 29-08-2022 at about 3.45 P.M.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 42 years.

The P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of the left rib 3rd to 8th ribs, fracture of the right humerus fracture with high radial nerve palsy.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 50% physical disability of right arm and for the whole body he has 17% physical disability.

The oral evidence of P.W.3 is fully corroborated with Devaraju .C vs Kempanna on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159118121/
6 documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary, Ex.P.19 case sheet,
Ex.P.20 x-rays (total 3), Ex.P.21 clinical examination report, Ex.P.22 x-ray and Ex.P.24 case-sheet clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered fracture of the left rib 3rd to 8th ribs, fracture of the right humerus fracture with high radial nerve palsy.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 29-08-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 11-10-2023, which is after lapse of one year and two months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, he has deposed that, the fractures sustained by the petitioner are united.
Further, he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner,
injuries sustained, duration of treatment and the oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Business Development Manager at K.12 Techno Service Private Limtied, Yeshwanthapura Central Office,
Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.47,000/- per month.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as Business Development Manager.
Therefore, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 42 years is 14.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 12/100 X 14 = Rs.3,12,480/-.

In the present case, the evidence on record clearly establishes that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. suffered fracture of the left rib 3rd to 8th ribs, fracture of the right humerus fracture with high radial nerve palsy.

viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 42 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of the left Devaraju .C vs Kempanna on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159118121/
8 rib 3rd to 8th ribs, fracture of the right humerus fracture with high radial nerve palsy.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.

Therefore,
awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
The cost of surgery for radial head replacement quoted by P.W.3 seems exaggerated.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,12,480-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,18,645-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 13,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 10,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,69,525/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-MB-4388 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,69,525/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,69,525/- (Rupees five lakh sixty nine thousand five hundred and twenty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is no evidence on record to show that,
the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner himself and not due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.
KA-50-MB-4388 and there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
16.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-50-MB-4388.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has caused due to self rash and negligent driving of petitioner and not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-50-MB-4388.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

injuries sustained, duration of treatment and the oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.

21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,12,480-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,18,645-00 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 13,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 10,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 4,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00
Total Rs. 5,69,525-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,69,525/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,69,525/- from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,69,525/- (Rupees five lakh sixty nine thousand five hundred and twenty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
